topic: Task/Agent tool API spec + YAML frontmatter

claims.claim: The Task tool was renamed to Agent tool in Claude Code v2.1.63; both names refer to the same underlying subagent spawn mechanism.
Subagent definitions live at ~/.claude/agents/ (user scope), .claude/agents/ (project scope), plugins, or via CLI flag; precedence is project > user > plugin > built-in.

Subagent frontmatter supports 17 fields: name, description, tools, disallowedTools, model, permissionMode, maxTurns, skills, mcpServers, hooks, memory, background, effort, isolation, color, initialPrompt, and the body content after YAML.

Five built-in subagent types exist: Explore (Haiku, read-only), Plan (inherit, read-only), general-purpose (inherit, all tools), statusline-setup (Sonnet, narrow tools), Claude Code Guide (Haiku, docs).
The description field is the most important routing signal - Claude uses it to auto-select which subagent to spawn; it should describe WHEN to run, not just WHAT.
tools is an allowlist; disallowedTools is a denylist; if tools is omitted the subagent inherits all parent tools; both together filter the set.
permissionMode values: default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions; plan mode makes the subagent read-only until approval.
model frontmatter accepts: sonnet, opus, haiku, haiku-fast, inherit, or specific model IDs; defaults to inherit.
maxTurns caps the subagent's tool-call loop iterations; prevents runaway spend.
AgentDefinition is the programmatic SDK type (Python + TypeScript) that mirrors the YAML frontmatter for runtime-constructed subagents.
Skills specified in frontmatter are loaded into the subagent's system prompt at spawn, but NOT applied when the same subagent definition runs as an Agent Teams teammate (documented asymmetry).
mcpServers frontmatter overrides which MCP servers are available to the subagent; also NOT applied when running as a teammate.
Invocation is natural-language via the main agent ('use the <name> subagent'), via explicit Agent tool call, or via slash command that references the subagent.
The isolation field controls context isolation between subagent and parent; defaults vary by spawn mode.
background: true in frontmatter is the declarative equivalent of the run_in_background pattern for subagents that should run asynchronously.
hooks frontmatter lets a subagent definition register its own lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/etc.) scoped to its invocations.

conflicts_flagged.description: Some community posts reference only a subset of frontmatter fields (older docs). v2.1.63+ canon is the 17-field set. Older tutorials may show 5-10 fields.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Default to v2.1.63+ canonical set; treat older posts as potentially stale.

gaps_flagged.description: isolation field semantics not fully documented - default behavior per spawn mode unclear.
background field schema relative to run_in_background Bash param not explicit.
Full payload of SubagentStart hook not published (SubagentStop is documented).
